candidate.answerReason: When \(n=-1\), adding the equations gives the contradiction \(0=3\). For every other real \(n\), the triple \(x=y=z=1/(n+1)\) satisfies all three equations.

methods.label: Construct a solution and isolate the exception
methods.explanation:
The equations have the same cyclic pattern, so try equal values \(x=y=z=t\). Each equation then becomes
\[
(n+1)t=1.
\]
For every real \(n\ne-1\), the denominator \(n+1\) is nonzero, and choosing
\[
x=y=z=\frac1{n+1}
\]
makes every left side equal to \((n+1)/(n+1)=1\). Thus the system has a solution for every such \(n\).

It remains to test \(n=-1\). Adding the three original equations gives
\[
(n+1)(x+y+z)=3.
\]
When \(n=-1\), this says \(0=3\), which is impossible. Therefore the system has no solution if and only if \(\boxed{n=-1}\), choice A.
methods.levelReason: Constructing and verifying a solution, then adding equations to obtain a contradiction in the exceptional case, uses elementary school algebra.

needsNewNodes.name: Common-solution existence in parameterized linear systems
needsNewNodes.description: Determine the parameter values for which simultaneous linear equations have at least one common real solution or no common real solution. A common solution must satisfy every equation; existence is distinct from uniqueness, and exceptional parameter values must be checked.
